content: Heads up: I’m currently upgrading live.lean-lang.org. Expect it to be broken until it has updated all its project cache files. (Thanks @Jon Eugster for the new version!)
Ah, already done. Please report any strange behavior to me. Or at least any new strange behavior.
It is now in light theme by default. I can switch it to dark theme, but this doesn't persist between tabs :(
A good change is that \ma now gives ↦ instead of ♂ :)
Same on https://lean.math.hhu.de/ or is the bug in my instance only?
That is also light theme by default for me
But does it persist?
(I think light was the default before as well.)
No, it doesn't persist there either.
Then I’ll pass that on to @Jon Eugster :-D
It persists for me when this flag is also enabled
Ah, thanks! It works now :)
(It does seem to take 0.5 seconds to before remembering that it needs to be in dark theme when opening a new tab, but that might not be new behaviour)
Hmm, I think it is new sadly

Some pre-existing issues I'd like to highlight now that we're on the topic:

  • Backslash+tab shortcuts for abbreviations add one or two extra spaces, instead of leaving the cursor right after the inserted character.
  • Cancellation of elaboration typically doesn't work. If I copy a large mathlib file into the editor and start typing at the top of the file, it has to fully elaborate every single version of the file. When that happens you have to refresh the page to continue.

My impression is that this sandbox (my pet name for live.lean-lang.org) runs in a protected environment on some remote system and just displays the results on my browser. So my computer should be relatively safe from all/most exploits involving untrusted code, as the interface has effectively no access to resources on my system. Is there documentation about this sandbox that confirms or refutes this? (Yes, this is an oversimplification; please correct me with more detail .)
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)

content:
This is true for any website as long as you don't click "allow" in any permission popups
(bar any bugs in your browser)

Please add bugs as issues on the repo: https://github.com/leanprover-community/lean4web

I do pick some there when I have time, but Ill forget about zulip conversations.

Using system default dark/light mode (and removing white flashing) is something that's on my list, but I didn't get around to fully implement it this time, it'll probably be in the next update. It's curious to me that it reportedly worked before, I don't think that's ever been implemented.

We now have “nightly (with mathlib)” on live:
https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=nightly-with-mathlib&codez=JYWwDg9gTgLgBAWQIYwBYBtgCMBQBiANwFMoBnYCAOyA

This tracks the nightly-testing-green branch of the mathlib4-nightly-testing repository.
